more.good_when: A maintainer who changes how the runner looks for what is left in the queue as it ends, keeping the behavior that a work added just as the runner ends still runs, sees every test still pass, as no test depends on how `queue.run` calls `queue.pending` inside it. Now test_a_work_added_just_as_the_runner_ends_still_runs replaces `queue.pending` by monkeypatch, which no caller of the queue does, so such a change fails that test while the behavior holds.

A maintainer who changes what a work records when its retries run out at the first stop changes one test, which asserts all that the case gives. Now two tests cover that same case on the same branch, test_a_work_with_no_retries_fails_at_its_first_stop in test_work.py and test_a_work_with_0_retries_fails_at_its_first_stop in test_overnight_command.py, and the second asserts only the exit code, stderr, and log, not its stdout or state.json.

When a work's `--dir` is gone by the time the work's turn comes, the user finds that work recorded as failed in the morning, with a log line saying the folder is missing, and finds the works after it run. Tried with ten works and the stand-in for `claude`: after `rmdir` of the second work's folder, the runner raised FileNotFoundError into runner.log, the work stayed `"status": "running"` with only `run 1 started` in its log, and no later work ran. `overnight` with no work given then stopped on the same work again, so the rest of the night never ran.
